research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic research-source confidence only: official GOV.UK, Natural England, Forestry Commission, National Highways and Planning Data authority; current-page availability, 2026 collector/update state where present, legal/process separation, mapped-vs-site-specific exactness, and funding/assessment-vs-permission/delivery controls. Not parcel-level accuracy.

official_sources.name: Agricultural land: assess proposals for development
official_sources.fact: Natural England guidance explains how planning authorities and developers should consider best and most versatile agricultural land in development proposals.
official_sources.gate: Policy relevance does not establish the exact ALC grade of a target parcel; detailed site evidence may still be required.

official_sources.name: Guide to assessing development proposals on agricultural land
official_sources.fact: The guide defines BMV as grades 1, 2 and 3a, requires Natural England consultation in specified 20ha-plus cases, and warns regional ALC maps are not accurate enough for individual fields or sites.
official_sources.gate: Regional ALC mapping must not be promoted to exact parcel grade; use post-1988 survey evidence or a detailed survey where necessary.

official_sources.name: Planning Data agricultural land classification
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 585 ALC geographies; the collector ran 22 July 2026 but the platform states the dataset was created by MHCLG and is intended to be replaced by authoritative-source data when available.
official_sources.gate: Current collector activity does not make the platform geometry authoritative Natural England site-survey evidence.

official_sources.name: Natural environment planning guidance
official_sources.fact: Planning guidance states grades 1, 2 and 3a are best and most versatile agricultural land and that decisions should take account of its economic and other benefits.
official_sources.gate: A policy definition is not a measured parcel ALC result.

official_sources.name: Air quality planning guidance
official_sources.fact: Planning guidance requires relevant development decisions to consider baseline air quality, development effects, sensitive users and mitigation where air quality is material.
official_sources.gate: AQMA or model context alone does not prove a parcel-specific concentration or planning outcome.

official_sources.name: Air pollution and development advice for local authorities
official_sources.fact: Natural England standing advice sets a staged assessment for air-pollution effects on protected sites, including critical loads/levels, in-combination effects and detailed assessment where needed.
official_sources.gate: Standing advice is a decision framework, not evidence that an exact development passes habitats or air-quality assessment.

official_sources.name: Planning Data air quality management area
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 498 AQMA geographies from authoritative sources; its collector ran 21 July 2026 and new data was last found 15 April 2026.
official_sources.gate: AQMA intersection is a planning consideration, not a measured site concentration or automatic refusal.

official_sources.name: Noise planning guidance
official_sources.fact: Planning noise guidance says numerical criteria in referenced assessment guidance are not fixed universal thresholds that must be achieved in every circumstance.
official_sources.gate: Noise suitability requires context and proposal-specific assessment; a generic threshold cannot be used as an automatic parcel score.

official_sources.name: When is permission required - Article 4 directions
official_sources.fact: Government guidance explains that Article 4 directions can withdraw specified permitted development rights and that a direction means a planning application is required, not that development is prohibited.
official_sources.gate: Article 4 status must not be converted into refusal or permission; exact direction scope and affected right must be checked.

official_sources.name: Planning Data article 4 direction area
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 7,133 Article 4 direction areas from 110 providers; the collector and new-data date are 22 July 2026, while some data is MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement.
official_sources.gate: Platform geometry must be reconciled to the exact live direction/document before changing permitted-development status for a parcel.

official_sources.name: Tree Preservation Orders and trees in conservation areas
official_sources.fact: Government guidance explains TPOs protect specified trees, groups or woodlands and generally require local authority written consent for prohibited works unless an exception applies.
official_sources.gate: A TPO is a tree-work control, not a blanket planning refusal or proof that all trees within a mapped vicinity are protected.

official_sources.name: Planning Data tree preservation order specification
official_sources.fact: The Planning Data specification updated 10 April 2026 defines linked order, zone and individual-tree datasets and requires authoritative order/document references and geometry/point fields.
official_sources.gate: Specification compliance improves structure but does not establish that a local record is legally current or spatially exact.

official_sources.name: Planning Data tree preservation zone
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 94,023 tree-preservation zones from 79 providers with collector/new-data dates of 22 July 2026; some data is MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement.
official_sources.gate: Zone overlap is screening evidence; verify the live order, order status and exact protected tree/group before parcel scoring.

official_sources.name: Trees and woodland guidance for local authorities
official_sources.fact: Forestry Commission guidance updated 17 July 2026 groups current resources for planning, planting and protecting trees and woodland, including TPO and woodland-protection material.
official_sources.gate: A guidance resource is not a site-specific forestry consent, felling licence or tree survey.

official_sources.name: Travel Plans, Transport Assessments and Statements
official_sources.fact: Planning guidance says developments generating significant movement should use proportionate Travel Plans, Transport Statements or Transport Assessments to assess and mitigate transport effects.
official_sources.gate: Network proximity or a generic accessibility measure cannot replace proposal-specific trip generation, capacity and mitigation evidence.

official_sources.name: NPPF chapter 9 promoting sustainable transport
official_sources.fact: Current NPPF transport policy requires early consideration of movement and network impacts and a vision-led approach to sustainable transport solutions.
official_sources.gate: Policy support for sustainable transport is not proof an exact development has acceptable residual highway impacts.

official_sources.name: Strategic road network and the delivery of sustainable development
official_sources.fact: DfT Circular 01/2022 describes how National Highways engages in plan-making and decision-taking while protecting safe and efficient operation of the strategic road network.
official_sources.gate: Nearby SRN infrastructure is not evidence of capacity, access approval or National Highways acceptance for a particular site.

official_sources.name: Environmental Impact Assessment planning guidance
official_sources.fact: Government EIA guidance distinguishes Schedule 1 and Schedule 2 development and explains when an Environmental Statement and planning application are required.
official_sources.gate: EIA screening/scoping or submission is not planning permission and must not be treated as environmental acceptability.

official_sources.name: Planning obligations guidance
official_sources.fact: Planning obligations are legally binding mitigation mechanisms and must satisfy necessity, direct relationship, and fair/reasonable scale-and-kind tests; guidance also separates education/infrastructure need from site-specific obligation justification.
official_sources.gate: An identified infrastructure need or formula does not prove a final S106 amount, executed agreement or delivered infrastructure.

official_sources.name: Publish your developer contributions data
official_sources.fact: Guidance requires relevant authorities to publish infrastructure funding statements and structured developer-contribution data.
official_sources.gate: Recorded or forecast contribution data is not proof that money has been received, spent or that infrastructure is operational.

official_sources.name: Viability planning guidance
official_sources.fact: Current viability guidance sets principles for plan-making and decision-taking and requires policy costs such as housing and infrastructure to be considered realistically.
official_sources.gate: A viability assessment is evidence for decision-makers, not a guaranteed permission, land value or funding outcome.

official_sources.name: Delivering schools to support housing growth
official_sources.fact: Department for Education guidance supports estimating pupil yield and securing developer contributions for education associated with housing growth.
official_sources.gate: A pupil-yield estimate or contribution formula is not proof that school places are funded, consented, built or available on occupation.
